Hi Jill — thanks, and welcome. I copied Kimberly (procurement) and Ben (vendor compliance) so we can give a single checklist for PO activation. Short answers up front: a dated CP575 plus a fully completed W-8BEN-E is usually acceptable; we treat a notarized signature as strongest evidence. The video can be accepted as an alternative in combination with a government-issued photo ID if the notary path is not possible.

Next steps I need from you to move to PO creation:
- Final signed page of the W-8BEN-E (scanned or DocuSign). If using DocuSign please send the envelope link.
- Supporting evidence (one of): CP575 IRS letter, bank letter on bank letterhead confirming legal entity and TIN, or an equivalent government tax registration document.
- If you prefer remote signatory validation instead of notarization: a short video (15–30s) of the signatory saying their name, title, and signing date while holding government ID next to the camera; provide the ID front only, redacting SSN if present.
- Billing entity name, remittance address, and preferred payment method (ACH or wire).

Timing: once we have the signed W-8BEN-E + one supporting evidence doc and the billing info, procurement can draft a PO. Typical turnaround is 3–5 business days from complete submission, assuming no follow-up questions.

We also have an internal hybrid pathway that speeds approval for international suppliers: notarization OR CP575 + signatory video + ID + DocuSign. Ben, can you confirm any compliance caveats?

Best,
